Piṭṭhiduka (The Supplementary Couplets)
Section on Analysis (Vibhaṅgavāra):

Condition by Way of Root (Hetupaccaya). Dependent upon a state to be abandoned by seeing, a state to be abandoned by seeing arises by way of root condition: dependent upon one aggregate to be abandoned by seeing, three aggregates arise ... [and so on] ... dependent upon two aggregates ... [and so on] ...

Dependent on a state to be abandoned by vision (*dassanena pahātabba*), a state not to be abandoned by vision arises by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*): dependent on the aggregates to be abandoned by vision, mind-produced matter (*cittasamuṭṭhāna-rūpa*) arises.

Dependent on a state to be abandoned by vision, both states—to be abandoned by vision and not to be abandoned by vision—arise by way of the root condition: dependent on one aggregate to be abandoned by vision, three [aggregates]...

The aggregates and mind-originated [matter] … two aggregates … [and so on] … Dependent on a state not to be abandoned by insight, a state not to be abandoned by insight arises by way of root condition:
dependent on one aggregate not to be abandoned by insight, three aggregates and mind-originated matter arise … two aggregates … [and so on].
…pe… at the moment of rebirth-linking …pe… dependent on the aggregates, there is the [heart-]base; dependent on the [heart-]base, there are the aggregates; one great primary element …pe….

Dependent on states both abandonable by vision and not abandonable by vision, a state not abandonable by vision arises by way of root condition: dependent on aggregates abandonable by vision and great primary elements …pe….
Matter produced by mind. (Abbreviated.
Chapter on Enumeration:
Pure.
In the case of the root condition, there are five; in the object condition, two; in the predominance condition, five; in the proximity condition, two; in the contiguity condition, two;

in the conascence condition, five; in the mutuality condition, two; in the dependence condition, five; in the strong-dependence condition, two; in the prenascence condition, two; in the repetition condition, two; in the kamma condition, five; in the resultant condition, one;
in the nutriment condition, five …pe… in the non-disappearance condition, five.
2.13.1.1.2. Negative Exposition of Conditions:
The Section on Analysis (Vibhaṅgavāra) – Not-root (Nahetu)

Dependent on a state to be abandoned by vision (*dassanena pahātabba*), a state to be abandoned by vision arises by way of the not-root condition (*nahetupaccaya*): dependent on the aggregates accompanied by doubt, delusion accompanied by doubt arises.
Dependent on a state not to be abandoned by vision, a state not to be abandoned by vision arises by way of the not-root condition:
dependent on one rootless aggregate not to be abandoned by vision ... [etc. ... at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking ... [etc. ... up to the non-percipient beings.
Dependent on aggregates associated with restlessness, arises delusion associated with restlessness.
Section on Enumeration:
Pure.
With not-root condition, two; with not-object condition, three; with not-predominance condition, five; with not-proximity condition, three; with not-contiguity condition, three;
with not-mutuality condition, three; with not-strong-dependence condition, three; with not-prenascence condition, four; with not-postnascence condition, five; with not-repetition condition, five;
with not-kamma condition, two; with not-resultant condition, five; with not-nutriment condition, one; with not-faculty condition, one; with not-jhāna condition...

One [condition] with respect to root, one with respect to object, three with respect to association, two with respect to dissociation, three with respect to absence, and three with respect to disappearance. 2.13.1.2.
The Section on Conascence:
The other two enumerations and the section on conascence should also be performed.

Conditioned by one aggregate to be abandoned by abandoning, there arise three aggregates and mind-produced matter … pe … conditioned by two aggregates … pe … at the moment of rebirth-linking … pe … (down to) internal great primaries;

conditioned by the [heart-]base, there arise aggregates to be abandoned by insight. Conditioned by a state to be abandoned by insight, a state to be abandoned by seeing arises by way of root condition: conditioned by the [heart-]base, there arise aggregates to be abandoned by seeing.
Conditioned by a state to be abandoned by seeing, there arise states both to be abandoned by seeing and not to be abandoned by seeing, by way of root condition:
conditioned by the [heart-]base, there arise aggregates to be abandoned by seeing; conditioned by the great elements, there arises mind-produced [matter].
Conditioned by states both to be abandoned by seeing and not to be abandoned by seeing,
a state to be abandoned by seeing arises by way of root condition: conditioned by one aggregate to be abandoned by seeing and the [heart-]base,
three aggregates arise … pe … conditioned by two aggregates and … pe ….
Conditioned by states both to be abandoned by vision and not to be abandoned by vision,
there arises a state not to be abandoned by vision by way of root condition: conditioned by aggregates to be abandoned by vision and the great elements,
mind-produced matter arises.
Conditioned by states both to be abandoned by seeing and not to be abandoned by seeing,
there arise states both to be abandoned by seeing and not to be abandoned by seeing, by way of root condition:

conditioned by one aggregate to be abandoned by seeing and the [heart-]base, three aggregates arise … pe … conditioned by two aggregates … pe … conditioned by [the five] aggregates to be abandoned by seeing … pe … [and so forth].
With the aggregates and the great primary elements as conditions, mind-originated matter [arises].
Section on Enumeration:
Pure.
In the cause condition, nine; in the object condition, four; in the predominance condition, nine … pe … in the non-disappearance condition, nine.
2.13.1.3.2. Negative Exposition of Conditions: The Section on Analysis.

Conditioned by a state eradicated by vision, a state eradicated by vision arises by way of the not-root condition: conditioned by the aggregates associated with doubt, delusion associated with doubt arises.
Conditioned by a state not eradicated by vision, a state not eradicated by vision arises by way of the not-root condition: [conditioned by] the rootless...
Conditioned by one aggregate to be abandoned by insight, there arise three aggregates and mind-produced matter … two aggregates … [and so on] up to non-percipient beings;
conditioned by the eye-base, eye-consciousness arises … conditioned by the body-base, body-consciousness arises;
conditioned by the [heart-]base, rootless aggregates to be abandoned by insight arise.
Conditioned by aggregates associated with restlessness, arises delusion associated with restlessness; conditioned by the [heart-]base, arises delusion associated with restlessness.
Conditioned by a state abandonable by vision, a state abandonable by vision arises by way of not-root condition: conditioned by the [heart-]base, arises delusion associated with doubt.
Conditioned by a state both abandonable by vision and not abandonable by vision, a state abandonable by vision...
A state arises without the root-condition: with doubt-accompanied aggregates and the [heart-]base as condition, doubt-accompanied delusion arises.
Chapter on Enumeration:
Pure.

In the absence of root condition, four; in the absence of object condition, three; in the absence of predominance condition, nine; in the absence of proximity condition, three; in the absence of contiguity condition, three;

in the absence of mutuality condition, three; in the absence of strong-dependence condition, three; in the absence of prenascence condition, four; in the absence of postnascence condition, nine; in the absence of repetition condition, nine;

in the absence of kamma condition, four; in the absence of resultant condition, nine; in the absence of nutriment condition, one; in the absence of faculty condition, one; in the absence of jhāna condition...

One [condition] with respect to root, one with respect to object, three with respect to association, two with respect to dissociation, three with respect to absence, and three with respect to disappearance. 2.13.1.4.
The Section on Support (Nissaya-vāra):
The other two enumerations and the section on support should also be performed.
2.13.1.5. Chapter on Conjoined States (Saṃsaṭṭhavāra) 2.13.1.5.1–4. Positive Conditionality, etc.
A state to be abandoned by seeing, being conjoined with [it], gives rise to a state to be abandoned by seeing by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.)
A state to be abandoned by insight is associated with a state to be abandoned by insight; such a state arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.
Two under root, two under object, two under predominance, (two in all cases), one under result …pe… two under non-disappearance.
Positive.

A state to be abandoned by vision arises in association with a state to be abandoned by vision through the condition of not-root: delusion accompanied by doubt arises in association with the aggregates accompanied by doubt.
A state not to be abandoned by vision arises in association with a state not to be abandoned by vision through the condition of not-root. (Abbreviated.)

With not-root condition: two; with not-predominance: two; with not-prenascence: two; with not-postnascence: two; with not-repetition: two; with not-kamma: two; with not-resultant: two; with not-jhāna: one; with not-path: one; with not-dissociation: two. The Negative (Paccanīya). 2.13.1.6.
The Chapter on Association (Sampayutta-vāra).
In the same way, the other two [methods]—counting and the application of associated factors—should also be performed. 2.13.1.7.
Chapter on Questions (Pañhāvāra). 2.13.1.7.1.
Positive Conditionality (Paccayānuloma).
Section on Analysis (Vibhaṅgavāra):
A state to be abandoned by seeing is a condition, by way of the root-condition, for a state to be abandoned by seeing... [three].
A state to be abandoned by non-seeing is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state to be abandoned by non-seeing:
roots to be abandoned by non-seeing are a condition, by way of root-condition, for their associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter;
at the moment of rebirth-linking … pe … .
A state to be abandoned by seeing is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state to be abandoned by seeing:
one relishes and delights in lust to be abandoned by seeing; taking that as object, lust to be abandoned by seeing arises.
Wrong view ... [and so on] ... doubt arises; grief to be abandoned by seeing arises.
One relishes and delights in wrong view to be abandoned by seeing; with that as object, lust to be abandoned by seeing arises, as do wrong view ...
[and so on] ... doubt ... [and so on] ... grief. With doubt as object, doubt arises.
...view arises... [and so on] ...grief arises. Taking as object the grief to be abandoned by seeing, there arises grief to be abandoned by seeing, view arises, and doubt arises.
A state to be abandoned by seeing is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state not to be abandoned by seeing: [as in the case of] the Noble Ones...
They review the defilements abandoned through seeing; they review [past] conduct previously practiced...

[and so on] ...they practice insight into the aggregates abandonable by seeing as impermanent... [and so on] ...by means of the knowledge of penetration of others' minds, they know the mind of one possessing a mind abandonable by seeing;
the aggregates abandonable by seeing are the object of the knowledge of penetration of others' minds and the knowledge of recollection of past lives.
Knowledge of the destiny of beings according to their deeds, knowledge of future states, and adverting consciousness are related to [their respective objects] by way of object-condition.
A state to be abandoned by insight (not by vision) is related to a state to be abandoned by insight by way of object-condition:
having performed an act of giving... morality... or the observance-day duties, one reviews it, enjoys it, and delights in it.
Taking that as an object, lust to be abandoned by non-seeing arises; restlessness ... pe ... sorrow to be abandoned by non-seeing arises.
[Or] having emerged from former well-performed deeds ... pe ... from jhānas ... pe ... the Noble Ones, having emerged from the path, review the path ... pe ...
[it is] a condition for the adverting to the fruit by way of object-condition; the Noble Ones, through non-seeing ... pe ... [it is] a condition.
They review the defilements that have been abandoned, the defilements that have been suppressed, ... [as before] ... the eye, ... [as before] ... the physical basis;
they contemplate with insight the aggregates abandonable by non-seeing as impermanent, ... [as before] ... they relish them and delight in them.
Taking that as an object, lust abandonable by non-seeing arises, as do restlessness, ... [as before] ... [the defilement] abandonable by non-seeing.
mental distress arises; one sees a form with the divine eye ... [and so on] ... it is a condition, by way of object-condition, for the knowledge of future states and for advertence.
A state to be abandoned by vision is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state to be abandoned by vision: [as in the case of] a gift.
... [as before] ... virtue ... [as before] ... the observance-day ceremony ... [as before] ... former [states] ... [as before] ... the jhānas ... [as before] ... the eye ... [as before] ...
one relishes and delights in the aggregates that are to be abandoned by vision with respect to the physical basis;
taking that as an object, lust to be abandoned by vision arises, as do wrong view ... [as before] ... doubt ... [as before] ... and grief to be abandoned by vision arises.
A state to be abandoned by seeing is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for a state to be abandoned by seeing: as object-predominance and as conascence-predominance.
Object-predominance: one esteems and delights in lust to be abandoned by seeing.
One rejoices; honoring that [object], lust to be abandoned by seeing arises, and wrong view arises.
Honoring that wrong view... [etc. ...Conascence-predominance: a predominance to be abandoned by seeing is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for the associated aggregates.
A state to be abandoned by seeing is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for a state not to be abandoned by seeing.
Co-nascent predominance: a predominance to be abandoned by seeing is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for mind-produced matter.
A state to be abandoned by seeing is [a condition] for both a state to be abandoned by seeing and a state not to be abandoned by seeing...
A state is related to a state by way of predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*). Co-nascent predominance:
a predominance to be abandoned by vision is related to its associated aggregates and to mind-produced matter by way of predominance condition.
A state not to be abandoned by vision is related to a state not to be abandoned by vision by way of predominance condition.
Condition: object-predominance and conascence-predominance. Object-predominance:
[having performed] giving … precept … the observance-day ceremony … [or having reflected on] the past … after emerging from jhāna, one esteems the jhāna, reviews it, enjoys it, and delights in it;
esteeming it, lust to be abandoned by seeing arises. The Noble Ones, after emerging from the Path, esteem the Path … [and so forth].
By treating it as venerable … [as above] … it is a condition for the fruit by way of predominance-condition (*adhipati-paccaya*).

By treating the eye … [as above] … or the physical basis (*vatthu*) as venerable, one relishes and delights in the aggregates (*khandha*) that are to be abandoned by non-seeing (*nadassanena pahātabba*);

by treating that as venerable, lust to be abandoned by non-seeing arises. Conascent predominance (*sahajātādhipati*): predominance to be abandoned by non-seeing is a condition for the associated aggregates.
And it is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for mind-originated material phenomena.
A state abandonable by seeing is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for a state abandonable by seeing.
As object-predominance: having given a gift ... pe ... [having attained] jhāna ... pe ... the eye ... pe ... the physical basis [for the mind], [is a condition] for states not abandonable by seeing.
Taking the aggregates as important, one relishes them and delights in them; taking them as important, lust to be abandoned by vision arises, and wrong view arises.
Immediately after...
A state to be abandoned by vision is a condition for a state to be abandoned by vision by way of proximity-condition:
preceding aggregates to be abandoned by vision are a condition for succeeding aggregates to be abandoned by vision by way of proximity-condition.
A state to be abandoned by seeing is a condition, by way of proximity-condition, for a state not to be abandoned by seeing:
aggregates to be abandoned by seeing are a condition, by way of proximity-condition, for emergence. (The root should be formulated.
Preceding aggregates not to be abandoned by seeing ... [and so on] ... are a condition, by way of proximity-condition, for the attainment of fruition.
(The Root should be made. Advertence is a condition for the aggregates to be abandoned by vision by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*).

It is a condition by way of contiguity-condition (*samanantara-paccaya*) … five [ways] … by way of mutuality-condition (*aññamañña-paccaya*) … two [ways] … by way of dependence-condition (*nissaya-paccaya*) … seven [ways].
Strong-dependence (*upanissaya*): … [to be completed].
A state to be abandoned by seeing is a condition, by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*), for a state to be abandoned by seeing:
as object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, and natural decisive support … [as above] … Natural decisive support:

relying on lust to be abandoned by seeing, one kills a living being … [and so on] … one causes a schism in the Saṅgha; [relying on] hatred to be abandoned by seeing … delusion to be abandoned by seeing … [and so on].
… relying on a view … or a wish, one kills a living being … [and so on] … causes a schism in the Saṅgha;
lust to be abandoned by seeing … [and so on] … a wish is a condition, by way of decisive support condition, for lust to be abandoned by seeing … [and so on] … for a wish.
A state to be abandoned by seeing is a condition, by way of decisive support condition, for a state not to be abandoned by seeing.
Condition: proximity-predominance condition, natural-predominance condition ... [etc. ... Natural-predominance condition:
depending on lust to be abandoned by seeing, one gives a gift ... [etc. ... one arouses an attainment. Depending on hatred to be abandoned by seeing ...
delusion ... wrong view ... longing, one gives a gift ... [etc. ... one arouses an attainment. By seeing ... [etc. ...
Lust to be abandoned by seeing … [and so on] … aspiration is related to confidence … [and so on] … to wisdom;

to lust, hatred, delusion, conceit, and aspiration to be abandoned by seeing; to bodily pleasure … [and so on] … and to the attainment of fruition, it is a condition by way of decisive support condition (upanissaya-paccaya).
A state to be abandoned by non-seeing is a condition, by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*), for a state to be abandoned by non-seeing:
as object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, natural decisive support … [as follows] … Natural decisive support:
relying on faith, one gives a gift … [and so on] … one arouses meditative attainment, conceives pride; [relying on] virtue … [and so on] … wisdom.
By means of non-seeing, one abandons lust, hatred, delusion, conceit, longing, bodily pleasure...
[and so on] ...relying upon a lodging, one gives a gift... [and so on] ...arouses an attainment, conceives conceit; [or] faith... [and so on] ...wisdom.
By means of non-seeing, one abandons lust... [and so on] ...longing, bodily pleasure... [and so on] ...the lodging.
Faith ... pe ... wisdom is related to lust abandonable by insight, ... pe ...
to aspiration, to bodily pleasure, to bodily pain, to the Path, and to the attainment of fruition, by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).
A state abandonable by insight is related to a state abandonable by vision by way of decisive support condition.
Condition: object-strong-dependence, proximity-strong-dependence, natural strong-dependence …pe…. Natural strong-dependence:
depending on faith, one adopts wrong view; depending on virtue …pe… depending on wisdom, one adopts wrong view;
[depending on] lust, hatred, delusion, conceit, wish, bodily pleasure …pe… lodging-place, which is not to be abandoned by seeing, [one adopts wrong view].
Depending on [an object], one kills a living being …pe… causes a schism in the Saṅgha;
faith …pe… and a lodging are related to lust, hatred, delusion, wrong view, and aspiration that are to be abandoned by seeing, by way of the decisive-support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).
Pre-arising (*purejāta*).
A state to be abandoned by non-seeing is a condition, by way of prenascence condition, for a state to be abandoned by non-seeing:
namely, object-prenascence and base-prenascence. Regarding object-prenascence:
the eye … [as before] … one contemplates the base as impermanent … [as before] … and enjoys it and delights in it; taking that as an object, lust to be abandoned by non-seeing arises.
... pe ... restlessness ... pe ... sorrow that is to be abandoned by not-seeing arises;
one sees a form with the divine eye, hears a sound with the divine ear-element. The visible-form base is [the condition] for eye-consciousness ... pe ...
the tangible-object base is [the condition] for body-consciousness ... pe .... Base-prenascence: the eye-base is [the condition] for eye-consciousness.

… pe … the body-base is a pre-arising condition for body-consciousness … pe … the physical basis (vatthu) is a pre-arising condition by way of pre-arising condition for the aggregates that are to be abandoned not by seeing.
A state to be abandoned not by seeing is a pre-arising condition for a state to be abandoned by seeing—namely, object-pre-arising and physical-basis pre-arising.
Object-pre-arising: the eye … pe … one relishes and delights in the physical basis; that [basis] is a condition.

A fine-material-sphere state is a condition for a fine-material-sphere state by way of root-cause condition (*hetupaccaya*). Fine-material-sphere roots are a condition for their associated aggregates by way of root-cause condition;
at the moment of rebirth-linking ... [the root should be supplied] ... Fine-material-sphere [roots].
Roots are related to mind-originated material phenomena by way of root condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking … [etc. … (The root section should be completed here).
Fine-material-sphere roots are related to their associated aggregates and to mind-originated material phenomena by way of root condition;
at the moment of rebirth-linking … [etc. …
A non-material-sphere state is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a non-material-sphere state:
non-material-sphere roots are a condition, by way of root-condition, for their associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter;
at the moment of rebirth-linking ... pe ... [end].
A fine-material-sphere state is a condition for a fine-material-sphere state by way of object-condition:

through the knowledge of penetration of minds, one knows the mind of one possessing a fine-material-sphere mind; fine-material-sphere aggregates [are conditions] for the knowledge of supernormal powers and the knowledge of penetration of minds.

The knowledge of recollection of past lives, the knowledge of passing away and rebirth according to karma, and the knowledge of future states are related to [their respective objects] by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*). A fine-material-sphere phenomenon is related to a non-fine-material-sphere phenomenon by way of object-condition:
one reviews the first jhāna … pe … one reviews the fourth jhāna; one reviews the divine eye.

He reviews the divine ear-element … the knowledge of the modes of supernormal power … the knowledge of penetration of minds … the knowledge of recollection of past lives … the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their deeds … the knowledge of future existences;
he reviews the aggregates of the fine-material sphere as impermanent … [and so on] … sorrow arises.
A non-material-sphere state is a condition for a non-material-sphere state by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*):
having given a gift, [one] reviews, relishes, and delights in the virtue ... the observance-day ritual ... or former well-performed deeds;
taking that as object, lust ... or grief arises. Furthermore, noble ones, having emerged from the path, review the path.
They review the fruit; they review Nibbāna. Nibbāna is related to change-of-lineage, purification, the path, the fruit, and adverting by way of object-condition.

Noble ones [review] defilements abandoned …pe… defilements suppressed …pe… [the past] …pe… the eye …pe… the basis, and the immaterial-sphere aggregates, as impermanent …pe… [as suffering, and as non-self].
... pe ... grief arises; the base of infinite space is related to the base of infinite consciousness ... pe ...
the base of nothingness is related to the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception ... pe ... the visible-form base is related to eye-consciousness ... pe ...
the tangible-object base is related to body-consciousness by way of object-condition.
A non-material-sphere state is a condition for a material-sphere state by way of object-condition: one sees a visible form with the divine eye;
one hears a sound with the divine ear-element; one knows the mind of one possessing a non-material-sphere mind by means of the knowledge of penetration of others' minds;
and non-material-sphere aggregates are conditions for the knowledge of supernormal powers, the knowledge of penetration of others' minds, and the knowledge of recollection of past lives.
It is a condition for the knowledge of the destination according to kamma and the knowledge of future existences by way of object-condition.
Predominance:
A fine-material-sphere state is a condition for a fine-material-sphere state by way of predominance-condition. Co-nascent predominance: the fine-material-sphere predominance.

It is a condition for the associated aggregates by way of the predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*). A fine-material-sphere phenomenon (*rūpāvacara-dhamma*) is a condition for a non-fine-material-sphere phenomenon by way of the predominance condition—namely, object-predominance (*ārammaṇādhipati*) and conascence-predominance (*sahajātādhipati*). Object-predominance:
one esteems, reviews, enjoys, and delights in the first jhāna; esteeming it, lust arises.
...a view arises ... [and so on] ... the fourth jhāna ... the divine eye ... the divine ear-element ...

knowledge of the modes of supernormal power ... knowledge of penetration of minds ... knowledge of recollection of past lives ... knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their kamma ...
knowledge of the future; having made that an object of esteem, one reviews it, relishes it, and delights in it, making that an object of esteem.
Lust arises; wrong view arises. Taking the fine-material-sphere aggregates as an object, one esteems them and delights in them;
taking them as an object, lust arises and wrong view arises. Conascence-predominance:

a predominance of the fine-material sphere is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for the material phenomena produced by consciousness. A fine-material-sphere phenomenon [is a condition] for a fine-material-sphere [phenomenon].
And a form-sphere state is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for a non-form-sphere state. Conascence-predominance:
a form-sphere predominance is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for its associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter.
A non-form-sphere state is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for a non-form-sphere state: namely, object-predominance (*ārammaṇādhipati*).

Co-nascent predominance. Object-predominance: having honored, one reviews, enjoys, and delights in a gift... morality... the observance-day rites... or former well-performed deeds; through honoring them, lust arises, wrong view arises.
Noble ones, having emerged from the path, honor the path... the fruit... Nibbāna... [and so on].
Taking it as an object of esteem, they review it: Nibbāna is a condition for the change-of-lineage, purification, the path, and the fruit by way of the predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*).
Taking the eye ... [and so on] ... the physical basis (*vatthu*), one esteems, relishes, and delights in the immaterial-sphere aggregates (*arūpāvacara-khandha*);
taking that as an object of esteem, lust arises, wrong view arises; one reviews the base of infinite space (*ākāsānañcāyatana*) taking it as an object of esteem.
... pe ... one esteems and reviews the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. Co-nascent predominance:
non-form-sphere predominance is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for its associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter.
Immediate, etc.
A fine-material-sphere state is a condition for a fine-material-sphere state by way of proximity condition:
preceding fine-material-sphere aggregates are a condition for succeeding fine-material-sphere aggregates by way of proximity condition.
A fine-material-sphere state is a condition for a non-fine-material-sphere state by way of proximity condition: a fine-material-sphere [state]...

a fine-material-sphere life-continuum is a condition for adverting [consciousness]... fine-material-sphere aggregates are a condition for a non-fine-material-sphere emergence by way of proximity-condition.
A non-fine-material-sphere state is a condition for a non-fine-material-sphere state by way of proximity-condition: preceding [states]...
Non-material-sphere aggregates are related to subsequent non-material-sphere aggregates by way of proximity condition (*anantara-paccaya*);

adaptation to change-of-lineage (*gotrabhu*), and so forth... the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is related to the attainment of fruition (*phala-samāpatti*) by way of proximity condition.
A non-material-sphere phenomenon is related to a material-sphere phenomenon by way of proximity condition—a non-material-sphere [phenomenon]...
Sense-sphere consciousness is a condition for fine-material-sphere rebirth-consciousness by way of proximity-condition;
non-material-sphere aggregates are a condition for fine-material-sphere emergence by way of proximity-condition;
the preparation for the first jhāna is a condition for the first jhāna by way of proximity-condition …pe… [and so on] up to the fourth jhāna.

... pe ... the preliminary work for the divine eye ... pe ... for the divine ear-element ... pe ... for the knowledge of the modes of supernormal power ... pe ... for the knowledge of penetration into others' minds ...
pe ... for the knowledge of recollecting past lives ... pe ... for the knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings according to their karma ... pe ...
for the knowledge of future existences is a condition for the knowledge of future existences by way of proximity-condition.
Conditioned by way of proximity condition … conditioned by way of conascence condition … seven … conditioned by way of mutuality condition … six … conditioned by way of dependence condition … seven.
Regarding decisive support:
A fine-material-sphere phenomenon is a condition for a fine-material-sphere phenomenon by way of decisive support condition—namely, as immediate decisive support.
Natural strong-dependence … [as above] … Natural strong-dependence: depending on fine-material-sphere faith, one produces a fine-material-sphere jhāna, higher knowledge … [and so on] … attainment;
depending on fine-material-sphere virtue … [and so on] … wisdom, one produces a fine-material-sphere jhāna … [and so on] … higher knowledge … [and so on] … attainment; fine-material-sphere [states].
Faith … pe … wisdom is a condition for fine-material-sphere faith … pe … wisdom by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).
The first jhāna is a condition for the second jhāna by way of decisive support condition;
the second jhāna is a condition for the third jhāna … pe … the third jhāna is a condition for the fourth jhāna by way of decisive support condition.

A fine-material-sphere state is a condition for a non-fine-material-sphere state by way of decisive support condition (upanissaya-paccaya)—namely, object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, and natural decisive support …pe…. As natural decisive support:
relying on a fine-material-sphere faith, one gives a gift, undertakes virtue …pe… performs the uposatha duty; [relying on] a fine-material-sphere jhāna …pe… insight.
... [and so on] ... the path ... [and so on] ... attainment, arouses conceit, or adopts a wrong view;
relying on fine-material-sphere virtue ... [and so on] ... wisdom, one gives a gift ... [and so on] ... arouses conceit, or adopts a wrong view;

fine-material-sphere faith ... [and so on] ... wisdom is related to non-fine-material-sphere faith ... [and so on] ... wisdom, to lust ... [and so on] ... to aspiration by way of decisive support (upanissaya).
… physical pleasure … physical pain … the Path, and the attainment of Fruition, are related to [their respective results] by way of decisive support condition (upanissaya-paccaya).
A non-material-sphere state is related to a non-material-sphere state by way of decisive support condition:
as object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, natural decisive support …pe…. Natural decisive support: having relied upon non-material-sphere faith …pe….
One gives a gift... [and so on] ...observes morality... [and so on] ...performs the Uposatha duty; one arouses a non-form-sphere jhāna...
[and so on] ...insight... [and so on] ...the Path... [and so on] ...attainment; one conceives conceit, adopts a wrong view;
one possesses non-form-sphere morality... [and so on] ...wisdom; one gives a gift depending upon lust... [and so on] ...food, or a lodging; one takes life... [and so on].

It kills … [and so on] … it causes a schism in the Saṅgha. Non-form-sphere faith … [and so on] … wisdom … lust … [and so on] … lodging is related to non-form-sphere faith … [and so on] … wisdom … lust … [and so on] … aspiration, bodily pleasure,
bodily pain, the Path, and the attainment of Fruition by way of decisive support condition (upanissaya-paccaya).

A non-material-sphere state is a condition for a material-sphere state by way of decisive support condition (upanissaya-paccaya)—namely, proximity-decisive support and natural decisive support … [as appropriate] … Natural decisive support:

relying on non-material-sphere faith, one arouses a material-sphere jhāna … [as appropriate] … higher knowledge … [as appropriate] … attainment; [relying on] non-material-sphere virtue … [as appropriate] … lodging.
Depending on [these], one arouses fine-material-sphere jhāna … higher knowledge … attainment.
Non-material-sphere faith … and lodging-place are related to fine-material-sphere faith … wisdom by way of decisive-support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).
The preparation for the first jhāna is related to the first jhāna by way of decisive-support condition … etc.

The preparation for the fourth jhāna …pe… the preparation for the divine eye …pe… the divine ear element …pe… the knowledge of the modes of supernormal power …pe… the knowledge of penetration into others’ minds …pe… the knowledge of recollecting past lives …pe… the knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings according to their kamma …pe… the preparation for the knowledge of future existences is a condition for the knowledge of future existences by way of decisive support condition (upanissaya-paccaya).
A non-material-sphere state that is pre-arisen, etc., is a condition for a non-material-sphere state by way of the pre-arisen condition: namely, object-pre-arisen and base-pre-arisen.
Object-pre-arisen: the eye … [and so on] … [contemplating] the base as impermanent … [and so on] … [giving rise to] grief.

Chapter on Enumeration:
Pure.

In the case of root-cause condition (hetu), there are four; in object condition (ārammaṇa), four; in predominance condition (adhipati), four; in proximity condition (anantara), four; in contiguity condition (samanantara), four;
in conascence condition (sahajāta), seven; in mutuality condition (aññamañña), six; in dependence condition (nissaya), seven; in strong-dependence condition (upanissaya), four;

in prenascence condition (purejāta), two; in postnascence condition (pacchājāta), two; in repetition condition (āsevana), three; in kamma condition (kamma), four; in resultant condition (vipāka), four; in nutriment condition (āhāra), four.
With respect to the faculties, there are four; with respect to the jhānas, four; with respect to the path, four; with respect to association, two; with respect to dissociation, three;
with respect to presence, seven; with respect to absence, four; with respect to disappearance, four; with respect to non-disappearance, seven. (The extraction of the negative.)
